items.label: AUDIO ESSAY 001
items.title: We Are All Archives Now
items.description: Historical archives began with the needs of the living. Today, our messages, photographs, and digital traces create records that circulate beyond us. What changes when artificial intelligence learns from what we leave behind?

narration.credit: Speech synthesis: CMU Flite 2.2 (open source), voice "slt". Text: Artificially Intelligent.
narration.disclosure: This is a demonstration recording with a synthetic voice from an open-source engine. It has not been reviewed and is not an approved narration.

article.basis: SHA-256 of the article's body paragraphs as published (narrated text) and of its Sources list.

checks.name: Transcript paragraphs equal the published article paragraphs, word for word
Sentences rebuild each paragraph exactly (only [n] citation markers are left unspoken)
Article text has not changed since narration
File is MP3, mono, 22.05 kHz, constant 48 kbps
Duration read back from the MP3 equals the recorded duration
SHA-256 of the file matches the record
Decoded length matches the timeline
Global timing offset between timeline and decoded MP3 is under 20 ms
Every gap between sentences is silent in the decoded MP3 (below -50 dBFS)
Every sentence interval contains speech in the decoded MP3 (above -45 dBFS)
Speech begins within 100 ms of where the timeline expects it (start + 30 ms lead-in)
Recording ends in silence rather than being cut off

notChecked: Pronunciation was checked only at the phoneme level (phones.py). No person has listened to this recording.
Prosody, emphasis and naturalness were not assessed.

Omissions are checked only as text: the transcript equals the article. That the voice actually says every word was not independently confirmed by speech recognition (no recogniser is available in the build environment).

items.label: AUDIO ESSAY 002
items.title: Is Human Consciousness Connected to Artificial Intelligence?
items.description: What if artificial intelligence is not separate from human consciousness, but a reflection of it? This article explores the relationship between the human mind and intelligent machines, and what that connection could reveal about memory, identity, awareness, and what it means to think.
